question: Rocket launch organisations learned from past launches. Which cut the chance of the next launch failing more: past successes or past failures?
answer: Past failures. Madsen and Desai studied orbital launches worldwide and found that organisations learned more from their failures than from their successes, and that knowledge from failures faded more slowly. A failure forces an investigation; a success is rarely taken apart to see why it worked.
move: Take apart a success as carefully as you would a failure.
ask: When did I last study why something went well, as carefully as I study what went wrong?
trap: Success seems to confirm what works, so it should teach more.
source: Madsen and Desai, Academy of Management Journal, 2010
reference: Madsen and Desai, Failing to learn? The effects of failure and success on organizational learning in the global orbital launch vehicle industry, Academy of Management Journal, 2010
